bull.b: Strong gross margins and materially improved free cash flow provide a better foundation for funding operations, content investment, and debt reduction. Although cash conversion has varied historically, the latest operating cash generation supports greater financial resilience over the next several quarters.

The sharp EBITDA margin improvement indicates that the business is benefiting from a more favorable digital mix and portfolio restructuring. If maintained, higher margins should increase cash generation from existing revenue, strengthen scalability, and support durable earnings improvement.

Debt repayment and reaffirmed targets show that management is directing improved cash generation toward balance-sheet repair. Continued deleveraging would reduce financial strain, improve capital-allocation flexibility, and make the company more resilient to operating or regulatory setbacks.

bear.b: The combination of substantial debt and persistent negative equity leaves Inspired with limited financial flexibility relative to its business size. Leverage can absorb a meaningful portion of operating cash flow, increase refinancing exposure, and constrain investment if performance weakens.

The higher U.K. duty directly reduces economics on gaming activity even while gross gaming revenue grows, creating a structural margin headwind in an important market. Further proposed tax changes could pressure both online and retail returns and complicate medium-term planning.

Recent revenue contraction and continued net losses weaken confidence that operating improvements will consistently translate into bottom-line earnings. Year-to-year profitability volatility also makes cash deployment and debt reduction more dependent on execution and favorable business conditions.
